exposure.uv_wavelength_nm: 390-400 (from the lamp's own marking, read 2026-08-09). Recorded as the stated range rather than collapsed to 395, because that is what is actually known. Cyanotype absorbs more strongly nearer 365, so this lamp does less work per watt - consistent with an SPE of 13:30 at 350mm. A replacement lamp at a different wavelength invalidates spe_seconds.
exposure.spe_note: read by eye from the 8-zone strip, dry: zones 6, 7 and 8 matched, zone 5 (9:30) still lighter, so the plateau begins at zone 6 = 13:30

measurements.note: Both halves off ONE coated sheet, so blocker and curve share a coating pass, exposure, wash and drying; they agree on density range to 0.052 log units where separate sheets disagreed by 0.19. Derived from the Photoshop-converted sRGB scans; the raw-linear route independently gave the same blocker and a curve differing by a mean of 0.005, so the colour-space handling is corroborated rather than assumed.

scan_settings.note: Scan SilverFast raw then convert to sRGB before analysis. Raw output is linear despite the embedded scanner profile advertising a 2.2 TRC; analysing the raw file needs space=linear, and the converted file needs no override. Both routes agree: the derived curves differ by a mean of 0.005 and both give hue 15 deg / sat 1.0.
